claim: Throat tension, exceeding the energy density: 4.8e42 Pa (MT88 eq. 51)
recomputed: tau(r0) = c^4/(8 pi G r0^2) = 4.815e+42 Pa from the sympy-derived p_l at r' = 0; independent of the shape and redshift functions when Phi' is finite
note: Applies to smooth throats. Thin shells carry surface stresses and flat-face portals carry the stress on line defects instead, so the number is model-class specific.

claim: Negative mass-energy present: ~-2e27 kg (about -1 Jupiter mass); Ellis, flat-face and thin-shell models
recomputed: Ellis -2.12e+27 kg (-1.11 M_J); flat-face rim of radius 1 m -2.12e+27 kg; thin shell -2.69e+27 kg (-1.42 M_J) (proper-volume integrals, both sides)
note: Model-specific, and not a requirement in general. The Misner-Sharp sum rule gives, per mouth, Int 4 pi r^2 rho dr = M_ADM - r0 c^2/2G: a light mouth needs -6.73e+26 kg (-0.35 M_J) per side, while a mouth heavier than r0 c^2/2G can have positive energy density everywhere (the NEC still fails through tension > density). All these configurations have zero Komar mass: they do not weigh -1 M_J.

claim: Negative-energy band thickness <~1e-21 m if supplied by free quantum fields (Ford & Roman 1996)
model: Morris-Thorne thin-band wormhole; flat-space massless-scalar QI, f = 0.01
recomputed: Generalised QI audit: thin exotic region of thickness a gives D ~ 8 (a/r0)^3 x 1.6e62; D = 1 at a = 9.20e-22 m (fitted slope 3.0)
note: Reproduced. Phase II adds: (i) smooth throats are excluded by D = 1.6e62 for any flare-out (boost-optimised bound), so a thin band is necessary, not optional; (ii) the band needs |rho| ~ 1.6e+64 J/m^3, 10^68 times the Casimir density at 1 um; (iii) slow travellers cross it with a tidal impulse of ~1 m/s.

claim: Stabilisation bandwidth faster than the 2.8 ns e-folding time (GGS 2009)
model: Massless Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole, linear radial perturbations
recomputed: Own derivation (delta-phi = 0 gauge), four methods: s = 1.1819727 c/b, e-folding 0.846043 b/c = 2.822 ns for b = 1 m
note: The control requirement is sharper than 'faster than the e-folding time': delayed PD feedback stabilises only if the loop delay is below sqrt(2)/s = 3.99 ns (proportional control alone never does), and the actuator must deliver NEC-violating stress. Parametric driving was tested and did not stabilise the full field equation.

note: True within classical or semiclassical spacetime without closed timelike curves (Lorentzian topology change needs them: Geroch 1967). Not established in quantum gravity.

claim: Unstable in all explicit models; no controller can coordinate faster than light crosses the throat
